reason: The hypothesis cites no specific prior evidence, and its key premises regarding entropy stabilization, kinetic trapping by rapid cooling, and the catalytic benefits of homogeneity are presented as general principles without support from the cited passages.
premises: High configurational entropy stabilizes a homogeneous atomic distribution in high-entropy alloys at high temperatures.
Rapid cooling can kinetically trap this high-temperature homogeneous state, preventing phase segregation.
Atomic-scale homogeneity in noble metal alloys enhances catalytic active site density and effectiveness.
Phase segregation in noble metal alloys reduces catalytic performance.
